result.title: Simulating Infant Senses with Age-Tuned Networks
result.comment: 21 pages, 7 figures, 2 tables. Code and website: https://github.com/pikulsomesh/developmental-world-models and https://pikulsomesh.github.io/developmental-world-models/
result.summary: What a newborn sees, hears and feels, and how this changes month by month, has been measured sense by sense, with different methods and in different units. We bring these measurements together for the first two years of life and ask whether small neural networks tuned to a given age can turn them into a quick, inspectable simulation of sensory perception. Each sense's immaturity is written as a fixed, age-indexed filter on the input, and a small prediction network learns behind it over the first year. The filters alone reproduce the order in which the senses mature, by construction. The networks add what filters cannot: in vision they extract far less than their input allows at early stages (at the newborn stage a toy's position cannot be read out, $R^2 = 0.00$, against 0.57 for a network trained directly on the same input), and a critical period and perceptual narrowing emerge without being built in; in hearing they track what their input allows. The same filters drive the Baby Senses Lab, a free website that shows a user's own images and sounds as a baby of a chosen age might sense them. It is a research and teaching tool, not a diagnostic test.

AI.brief_summary: 论文汇总婴儿出生两年内各感官成熟度的测量数据，用固定的年龄索引输入滤波器加小型预测网络，构建可快速检视的感官知觉模拟，并做成展示网站。
AI.relevance_reason: 年龄索引滤波器限制输入可用信息（新生阶段位置不可读出，R²=0.00）从而约束内部状态可提取内容的做法，可能与 LVR 关注的视觉细节保留、信息坍缩以及训练课程与状态约束设计存在概念联系，可供核查。
